name: Safe zones for percutaneous pins or screws in the humerus
corridor: Open or mini-open pin corridors in the humerus with direct identification of the radial nerve, since percutaneous pin placement in the humerus is not safe

positioning.text: Position with the arm supported and accessible laterally, with imaging available to localize pin sites.

surface_landmarks.text: Identify the lateral humeral shaft and the course of the radial nerve as it crosses the posterolateral humerus.

incision.text: Use an open incision rather than percutaneous entry, large enough to insert pins and retract the radial nerve.

superficial_interval.text: Dissect down to bone under direct vision, identifying and protecting the radial nerve before drilling.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, the brachial fascia and muscle, the radial nerve, and the humeral cortex.

structures_at_risk.text: The radial nerve is the principal structure at risk and must be identified and protected before pin or screw insertion in the humerus.

danger_zones.text: The posterolateral humeral shaft where the radial nerve crosses is the danger zone; percutaneous placement here is unsafe.

retraction_hazards.text: Retract the radial nerve gently under direct vision during drilling and pin insertion.

exposure.text: Provides a controlled open corridor for humeral pins with the radial nerve protected.

limitations.text: Percutaneous humeral pin placement is not safe, so an open technique is mandatory and available corridors are limited by the radial nerve.

indications.text: Indicated for open placement of external fixator pins or screws in the humerus.

closure.text: Close the soft tissues loosely around each pin, ensuring the radial nerve is not tethered.

complications.text: The principal complication is radial nerve injury; pin-tract infection may also occur.

procedure_applications.condition: External fixator pins are placed in the humerus, for example for temporary spanning fixation

questions.question: Is percutaneous pin placement in the humerus considered safe?
questions.answer: No; an open technique with radial nerve protection is required.

questions.question: Which nerve must be identified before humeral pin insertion?
Why is a larger incision recommended for humeral pins?
questions.answer: To allow insertion of pins and retraction of the radial nerve under direct vision.
